served.stem: The product trans-2-methylcyclopentan-1-ol is desired from the alkene shown (1-methylcyclopentene), with the new OH placed on the LESS substituted alkene carbon. Which reagent sequence gives this anti-Markovnikov, syn-addition outcome?
served.bankWhy: Hydroboration-oxidation adds H and OH across the double bond anti-Markovnikov (OH to the less substituted carbon) and syn (H and OH add to the same face), which on a ring sets the trans relationship between the new OH and the adjacent methyl. Acid hydration and oxymercuration are both Markovnikov and would place OH on the more substituted carbon.

answer.line: Hydroboration is the one hydration that is both anti-Markovnikov and syn. Those two words are the whole stem.

steps: Ask the two questions: which carbon, and which face? The OH goes to the less substituted carbon, so anti-Markovnikov, and H and OH add to one face, so syn.
Boron goes to the less crowded carbon, and B and H add together in one step from one face. No cation forms, so nothing shifts.
H2O2 and NaOH swap boron for OH right where it sat. The new H and the OH are cis, which leaves the OH trans to the methyl.

choices.note: Oxymercuration skips the rearrangement, which is why it pulls. But it is Markovnikov: the OH lands on the methyl carbon and gives the tertiary alcohol.
Acid hydration runs through the tertiary cation. Markovnikov puts the OH on the methyl carbon, and a flat cation gives no face control.
HBr without peroxide puts Br on the tertiary carbon. NaOH on a tertiary bromide eliminates or gives the tertiary alcohol, never the secondary one.
Same Markovnikov address as any acid hydration, and heat pushes the equilibrium back toward the alkene.
Anti-Markovnikov and syn in one reagent: OH on the less substituted carbon, trans to the methyl.
